summary:
LOOP. test_full_pipeline.main (test_full_pipeline.py:454) owns the whole plan-act-sense loop. Phase 1 builds BoxelTestEnv (:481), settles 50 steps (:562) and runs an oracle_detect_objects pass that is print-only (:576). Phase 2 calls env.get_camera_observation (:610), which renders the fixed camera with ER_TINY_RENDERER, runs perception.detect_objects_from_render and builds OBJECT and SHADOW boxels from the ESTIMATES only (boxel_env.py:1655-1706, 1708-1761); free space is an octree over _SAFE_TABLE ranges (:1543-1568). Phase 4 is the harness's ground truth: oracle_detect_objects decides which targets are hidden and target_name = random.choice of the hidden ones (test_full_pipeline.py:692-732); for find_dice the target is the class 'dice', so this choice is moot, but the hidden/visible split still feeds the ORACLE log line only. The planner is PDDLStreamPlanner(registry, robot_id=env.plan_robot_id, shadow_occluder_map, physics_client=env.plan_client_id, object_body_ids, support_body_ids, camera_pos, tray_name) (:952-958); all IK/RRT/collision work runs on a SECOND DIRECT client that sync_to_plan_client poses from the BELIEF (registry centres, hidden bodies parked at (5,5,-5), robot joints by proprioception; boxel_env.py:698-766). Each iteration: reboxelize if dirty (:1298), sync (:1321), planner.plan (:1323), optional disposal plan with goal (handempty) when no plan while holding (:1375-1413), then a dispatcher over move/sense/pick/place/place_hiding/stack (:1490-2251). move re-solves plan_motion from the real arm pose (:1549) and streams waypoints with move_robot_smooth (:1583). sense is execution.handle_sense_action (execution.py:2412), which takes ONE render (:2495), classifies the named fragment with sense_shadow_from_render against depth+seg (:2513), registers a found target from the render (:2572-2599), registers every other newly visible body (register_new_detections :2255, with shadows cast by env.shadow_calculator :2356), re-poses known boxels (refresh_object_aabbs :1900, rigid-size, arm-occlusion guard, lost check), sweeps every fragment against the same render (sweep_all_fragments :2180), shrinks still_blocked fragments (:2135) and parks a fragment after 3 strikes (:3061-3079, :2718-2736). After every executed action _integrity_after (test_full_pipeline.py:1109) runs world_integrity_check (execution.py:1760, perception only) plus register_new_detections and replans on belief change. Exit reasons: all_searched (:1264), no_plan_while_holding (:1402), pick_giveup (:1436), no_plan_binding_death (:1447), planner_failed (:1456), knocked_off_table (:1154), stack_giveup (:2119), physics_mismatch (:2287, :2306), target_lost (:2324), and run_logger maps None to 'timeout' (run_logger.py:285-289; also drop_failed :337). Holding success = belief.is_target_found() AND _verify_holding (ground-truth pad contacts, scoring only; :2275-2288); the loop itself stops when held_body_id == env.objects[target].object_id (:1197-1206).

DETECTION. perception.py is pure numpy: detect_objects_from_render(seg_mask, depth_buffer, view, proj, body_id_to_name, camera_xy, support_z, min_pixels=6, no_footprint_completion) unprojects each seg id's pixels to a cloud, takes its AABB, grows the shorter horizontal axis away from the camera (box-like near-square prior, :420-433) and lowers the bottom onto the highest support under its footprint or the table (_rest_on_support :441-494). It assumes a seg id to name map supplied by the caller (boxel_env excludes 'plane','table','robot' by NAME :1749-1752), a single support plane support_z, and nothing floating. The sense grid (sense_ray_slices :88) is one dense slice at base+0.02 m with 12 mm spacing plus two 7x7 slices; the comments bind these numbers to 3 to 4 cm targets (:39-56). The pure functions can run on any render; detect_objects itself is a BoxelTestEnv method needing self.objects (ObjectInfo), camera params, table_surface_height and client_id.

EXECUTION. execute_pick (execution.py:891) aims at the registry estimate, re-observes once before the descent (:998), descends in two stages with seeded solve_ik, sizes the pre-grasp aperture from the estimate (:1074), closes tactilely with close_gripper_until_contact (robot_utils.py:881, force 60 N, squeeze 3 mm), verifies both pads plus width plausibility (:1169-1231), retries once, lifts (hardcoded, default 0.10 m :869/:1246, not the ~5 cm the audit text says) and re-verifies the hold (:1255). execute_place/execute_stack derive the release height from the held object's rigid estimate (:1360, :1552), release through the motors with a tactile gate (fingers >= 0.038 and no robot contact, :632/:678), lift, then verify by observation (_observe_release :695) and mirror the belief into the plan client (:1453-1459, :1711-1716). Remaining simulator reads in execution are print-only diagnostics (:605-615, :657-661, :1129-1138, :1260, :1567-1580, :1629-1650) plus identity reads: env.objects[name].object_id to pick the contact body (:971) and getContactPoints(bodyA=robot, bodyB=obj_id) (:1169, :1255, :524). One privileged read survives in the model: shadow_calculator.calculate_shadow_boxel still raycasts the TRUE physics world to find shadow extents (shadow_calculator.py:160, default client), PAPER_AUDIT item (h).

COUPLING. Panda link indices 9/10/11 are hardcoded for pybullet_data's panda.urdf (robot_utils.py:22-24, also boxel_env.py:735/810/824, world_eye.py:47-49, telemetry.py:139); TAMPURA's Panda is models/srl/franka_panda/panda.urdf with extra named links camera_frame and panda_tool_tip resolved by NAME (robot.py:9-32, :122-123) and 0.045 m fingers (:130). Their camera is wrist-mounted and moved by 'look' actions (env.py:584-680), ours is a fixed external eye (0.1,-0.8,0.7) looking at (0.1,0,0.5), 640x480, fov 60 (boxel_env.py:442-482). Their table top is z=0 (panda_env_utils.py:709-713), ours z=0.325 (boxel_env.py:779-783); their objects spawn at x in [0.3,0.7], y in [-0.4,0.4] (env_generator.py:115-116) with the die co-located under an upside-down cup (:123-127) and a scene accepted only when the die is absent from the home-camera seg mask (:164-172). Our reach gates (REACH_LIMIT_M 0.80, sphere R 0.815 centred at WORLD z 0.066; streams.py:38-57) were measured for a base at z 0.05 and must be re-derived relative to their base. execution.py and robot_utils' motion/gripper functions call p.* WITHOUT physicsClientId (default client), so the bridge must make our physics world pybullet's first connection or thread the client id through (mechanical). TAMPURA opens two BulletClients (world and sim_world, env.py:822-826).

facts.claim: main() is the single orchestrator: Phase 1 env build and settle, Phase 2 observation to boxels, Phase 3 registry, Phase 4 oracle hidden split and goal formation, Phase 5 replan loop with inline dispatcher, Phase 6 scoring.

Initial perception: get_camera_observation renders once with ER_TINY_RENDERER on self.client_id, runs detect_objects_from_render, and generate_boxels builds OBJECT+SHADOW boxels from estimates only; objects without an estimate get no boxel.

oracle_detect_objects (true poses + 8-corner rayTestBatch body-id match) is still called in Phase 1 (print-only), Phase 4 (hidden split, target choice, ORACLE log), and the CLI pre-flight for find-and-tray-stack; it does not feed get_camera_observation.

The planner runs on a separate DIRECT plan client posed from the belief: static plane/table/tray at true pose, every other body at its registry boxel centre, bodies without a boxel parked at (5,5,-5), held body at the EE, robot joints copied from the executing robot.

PDDLStreamPlanner constructor signature: (registry, robot_id, shadow_occluder_map, physics_client, object_body_ids, support_body_ids, camera_pos, tray_name); plan() is called with target_objects, goal, current_config, known_empty_shadows, moved_occluders, max_time, visible_target_locations, on_relations, stackable_objects, unit_costs, planner, held_obj.
Loop termination for holding goals is a body-identity test: held_body_id (returned by execute_pick as env.objects[obj_name].object_id) == env.objects[target_name].object_id.

Exit reasons set in the loop: all_searched, no_plan_while_holding, pick_giveup, no_plan_binding_death, planner_failed, knocked_off_table, stack_giveup, physics_mismatch, target_lost; run_logger maps None to 'timeout' and also knows drop_failed.

handle_sense_action takes exactly one render per sense and reuses it for classification, target registration, new-body registration, rigid-size refresh with lost check, full-registry sweep, and (for still_blocked) the partial-reveal shrink; 3 still_blocked or 3 unlocalizable strikes park the fragment as unresolved (never marked empty).

sense_shadow_from_render classifies grid endpoints via first_surface_interceptors (depth in front of endpoint by > 3 mm) with the seg id naming the interceptor; the arm counts as a blocker; outcomes found_target / still_blocked / contains_nontarget / clear_but_empty; worst-slice fraction > 0.05 means still_blocked.

compute_shadow_blockers reads one render via env.detect_objects and lists a body as blocker only when removing it is needed to bring every slice under the 5 % tolerance; the shadow's creator is a fallback blocker only while its AABB still touches the fragment.

world_integrity_check is perception-only (env.detect_objects) and classifies knocked_off_table / lost / disturbed (>15 mm) / toppled / off_support (>20 mm); _integrity_after also registers newly visible bodies and replans on belief change when the hand is empty.

refresh_object_aabbs re-poses boxels with rigid-size tracking (per-axis max of known and estimated extents, XY on the estimate, z top-anchored), keeps the last estimate for bodies partly behind the arm (3x3x3 lattice test), and reports LOST when a stale body's region renders visible-through on every slice.

detect_objects_from_render signature: (seg_mask, depth_buffer, view_matrix, projection_matrix, body_id_to_name, camera_xy, support_z, min_pixels=DETECTION_MIN_PIXELS, no_footprint_completion=frozenset()); priors only grow the box: square-footprint completion away from the camera and support snap / rest-on-support.

Perception constants: DETECTION_MIN_PIXELS 6, DETECTION_SUPPORT_SNAP 0.02, SUPPORT_FOOTPRINT_MIN_FRACTION 0.25, SENSE_MARGINAL_BLOCKED_FRACTION 0.05, SENSE_LOW_SLICE_OFFSET 0.02, SENSE_DENSE_SPACING 0.012, SENSE_COARSE_N 7, SENSE_MAX_N_PER_AXIS 64, SENSE_RENDER_DEPTH_TOL 0.003; comments tie the 0.02 offset and 0.012 spacing to targets of half-extent >= 0.015 and footprint >= 0.03.

boxel_env.detect_objects builds body_id_to_name from env.objects excluding names 'plane', 'table', 'robot' and passes is_tray bodies as no_footprint_completion; the renderer is wrapped by conceal/restore overlay calls for the GUI debug viz.

Our fixed camera defaults: eye [0.1,-0.8,0.7], target [0.1,0.0,0.5], up z, 640x480, fov 60 deg, near 0.01, far 5.0; the table is pybullet_data table.urdf at [0.5,0,-0.3] with top z 0.325; the robot is pybullet_data franka_panda/panda.urdf at [-0.4,0,0].

Workspace windows: logical table_x_range (-0.4,0.6) / table_y_range (-0.5,0.5) feed ShadowCalculator; _SAFE_TABLE_X_RANGE (-0.1,0.70) / _SAFE_TABLE_Y_RANGE (-0.40,0.40) feed FreeSpaceGenerator, UniformGridGenerator and the on_surface annotation; _TABLE_PLACE ranges (-0.20,0.60)/(-0.50,0.50), _ROBOT_BASE_XY (-0.4,0.0), _PANDA_REACH_RADIUS 0.65 are spawn-time only.

ShadowCalculator still casts rays in the TRUE physics world (p.rayTestBatch from the believed object's back corners outward, default client unless physics_client is passed) to find where the shadow lands on the table; hit points are clamped to the table ranges.

Panda link indices are hardcoded for pybullet_data's panda.urdf: ARM_JOINT_INDICES 0-6, FINGER_JOINTS [9,10], END_EFFECTOR_LINK 11 (panda_grasptarget), _PANDA_IGNORED_SELF_PAIRS, _PANDA_GRIPPER_LINKS {6..11}; duplicated as literals in boxel_env (:735, :810, :824), world_eye (:47-49) and telemetry (ee_link=11).

Reach gate: REACH_LIMIT_M 0.80 horizontal from the base XY plus a sphere R 0.815 centred at (base_x, base_y, WORLD z 0.066); base XY read once from the plan client; the comment states the measured envelope is for a base reported at z 0.05 (centre 0.016 above base).

Grasp sampler: top-down only, yaw 0 or pi/2 by pinch axis, _GRASP_Z_OFFSETS [0.10, 0.06], GRASP_MAX_SPAN 0.076, GRASP_SQUARE_TOL 0.005, altitude gate z >= half_height + 0.01; pre-sense objects use NOMINAL_HIDDEN_EXTENTS (0.04 cube) and keep every offset; objects in ungraspable_objects get no grasp.

Class priors: NOMINAL_HIDDEN_EXTENTS [0.04]*3 for fits/place/stack half-height and the F15 sliver box; NOMINAL_HIDDEN_EXTENTS_MIN [0.03]*3 for hideability; both documented as '3-4 cm target cubes across all scenes'.
test_target_can_hide_in_shadow raycasts the PLAN client (belief-posed) and derives table_z as the min z of registered SHADOW boxels; it is used only under --sense-gate strict.

Octree min_resolution default 0.035 (free_space.py) is overridden at startup by auto_cell = max object extent (from ObjectInfo.size) + 0.01 unless --min-boxel-size is explicit; free space spans z up to table + 0.5.

execute_pick contact rule: contact_z = max(estimated top - 0.005, table_z + 0.035); pre-grasp aperture min(0.04, pinch_half + 0.008); tactile close force 60 N, squeeze 3 mm, table and plane ignored as pad contacts; grip requires both pads and measured half-width in [0.005, pinch_half + 0.008]; one retry; post-pick lift default 0.10 m; post-lift pad re-verify.

The post-action lift is the one exempted hardcoded motion; the code lifts 0.10 m after pick, place and stack (lift_height default, no override at the pick call), while the audit text and docstrings say ~5 cm after pick.

Release verification is tactile (fingers >= 0.038 after a 160-step 200 N motor open, zero robot-link contact, up to 3 attempts) followed after the lift by an observation check (top within 2 cm of expected, footprint within rigid + 1.5 cm, centre shift <= 3 mm between two renders); an unobserved object is accepted on the tactile checks.

execute_place / execute_stack take held_aabb / support_aabb estimates from the registry and compute release height from _grasp_ee_to_obj_z (the pick rule inverted); the plan client is updated from the release observation centre or the intended destination; entry requires both pads in contact (EmptyHandError otherwise).

Remaining ground-truth reads in execution.py are print-only diagnostics: pre-release pose/AABB/tilt, post-release bottom/tilt, pick arrival ee_vs_obj, obj_z on grip loss, stack support true top and held tilt, stack arrival deviation.

Static-body filtering is by hardcoded NAME ('plane','table','robot') and the is_tray attribute in at least 12 sites across boxel_env, execution and test_full_pipeline; target/occluder roles come from ObjectInfo.is_occluder set at spawn.

Execution-side p.* calls (contacts, joint states, link states, motor control, stepSimulation) carry no physicsClientId and therefore address pybullet's default client; only the plan-client mirror writes pass physicsClientId=env.plan_client_id. robot_utils IK/collision functions and detect_execution_collisions take a physics_client argument; move_robot_smooth, open_gripper, close_gripper, close_gripper_until_contact do not.
facts.evidence: execution.py (2 physicsClientId occurrences, :1457-1459, :1714-1716); robot_utils.py:675-936 vs 162-329, 429-504, 511-672; test_full_pipeline.py:179-180, 218, 283, 1574, 1592, 1870, 2107

facts.claim: RenderingLock is a process-global counter that assumes a single physics client.

Plan-client mirroring requires every body to be created through _mirror_load_urdf / _mirror_spawn_object so _gui_to_plan maps GUI ids to plan ids; register_new_detections and the found-target hook call env.plan_body_id (KeyError for unmirrored bodies).

Dispatcher-level retry policies that are not planner decisions: execute_pick one-shot grasp retry, F2 3-strike pick giveup with 2 paroles after 4 replans, transit-loss 3-strike, F9 rediscovery 3-strike, #21 still_blocked 3-strike park, F15 unlocalizable 3-strike park, disturbed-count cap of 3 per plan, disposal plan with goal (handempty), runtime plan_motion re-solve before each move.

The CLI pre-flight constructs the scene headlessly once before the real run (no seed re-roll) and for find-and-tray-stack uses oracle_detect_objects to check the visible/hidden role split; the comment notes seed lists for sweeps 'must be pre-vetted'.

Scoring verifiers read simulator truth: _verify_cube_on (AABBs), _verify_on_table, _verify_holding (held id equals target id, both pads, squeeze >= 0.5 N), _verify_goal_physics; the audit explicitly keeps them as harness scoring.
telemetry and world_eye read simulator truth for logging only; telemetry.enable(client_id, robot_id, body_names, run_dir) and world_eye.enable(run_dir, env, robot_id, body_id_to_name).

TAMPURA's Panda is models/srl/franka_panda/panda.urdf with named links camera_frame and panda_tool_tip resolved by name, joint groups by name, MAX_PANDA_FINGER 0.045, OPEN_GRIPPER_POS [0.045,0.045], DEFAULT_ARM_POS given; the URDF itself is not in either local mirror.
facts.evidence: robot.py:9-54, 107-160; panda_env_utils.py:844-851, 855; Glob for panda.urdf under git/tampura_environments returned nothing

facts.claim: TAMPURA's camera is mounted on the hand (Camera.get_pose = link pose of camera_frame), intrinsics 640x480 FX=FY=525, rendered with ER_BULLET_HARDWARE_OPENGL (tiny=False); 'look' actions move the arm to sampled camera poses 0.2 to 0.3 m above the object, and the sampler reads the TRUE pose of the object it looks behind.

TAMPURA's observation model maps seg-mask body ids to object symbols and returns their TRUE poses for every visible body; the belief tracks a 15 mm visibility grid over an AABB x in [0.37, table_upper-0.05], z in [top+0.02, top+0.1].

TAMPURA's find_dice scene: table box 1.53x1.22x0.03 at (0.1,0,-0.015) so the top is z=0 (shortened placement table 0.75x1.22 at x=0.475), robot base at the origin, 1 die plus 1 to 5 upside-down YCB cups with x in [0.3,0.7], y in [-0.4,0.4], random yaw; the die is placed at the last cup's position (co-location) and a scene is saved only when the die is absent from the home-camera seg mask; scenes are JSON files chosen by random.choice.
TAMPURA's reward (success) is holding the target die AND at-home; actions are pick, place, look, go-home, NoOp.

The archived v1 bridge placed a fixed external camera over the occluder centroid (explicitly not using the die pose) or used an eye-in-hand at home; this records the prior camera decision for the restart.
PAPER_AUDIT #P4 still lists open requirement (f): containment regions under cups are not modelled by lateral shadows, and (g): the arm park before sense was bridge-internal, not planned.

ObjectInfo.position is refreshed from true poses by env.update_object_positions after actions but the only consumer outside logging is the Phase 4 oracle log lookup; planning and execution read registry estimates.
facts.evidence: boxel_env.py:1856-1869; test_full_pipeline.py:696, 1734, 1845, 1906, 2153; grep over pddlstream_planner/reboxelize/belief/execution found no .position consumer

design_relevant_details: Loop entry: test_full_pipeline.main(gui, run_logger, scene_config, draw_boxel_overlays, show_free, goal_kind in {'holding','stack','find-and-tray-stack'}, stack_height, unit_costs, baseline, uniform_cell_size, min_boxel_size, run_config, telemetry_enabled, telemetry_period, telemetry_heartbeat) -> bool; it constructs BoxelTestEnv itself at :481 and reads the module-global `args` (max_plan_time, log_level, planner, sense_gate, corridor_test) at :961-969 and :1329-1349, so a bridge must either inject an env-like object or refactor main to accept one.

Duck-typed env surface the loop and execution use: client_id, plan_client_id, plan_robot_id, objects: Dict[str, ObjectInfo(object_id, name, position, orientation, size, is_visible, is_occluder, is_tray)] with mandatory keys 'plane','table','robot'; camera_position, camera_target, camera_up, image_width, image_height, fov, near_plane, far_plane; table_surface_height, table_x_range, table_y_range, _SAFE_TABLE_X_RANGE, _SAFE_TABLE_Y_RANGE; shadow_calculator, free_space_generator(.min_resolution), uniform_grid_generator, use_uniform_grid; methods detect_objects(), get_camera_observation(), _depth_buffer_to_meters(), _view_and_projection_matrices(), generate_boxels(est_aabbs), generate_free_space(known, visualize), annotate_free_space_surface(cells), sync_to_plan_client(held_body_id, registry), plan_body_id(gui_id), _gui_to_plan, step_simulation(n), update_object_positions(), oracle_detect_objects() (harness only), refresh_debug_camera_views(), close(), scene_config.n_hidden_targets / .seed.

perception.detect_objects_from_render(seg_mask, depth_buffer_raw01, view_matrix16, projection_matrix16, body_id_to_name, camera_xy, support_z, min_pixels=6, no_footprint_completion=frozenset()) -> Dict[name, ObjectDetection(name, body_id, pixel_count, est_min, est_max)]; depth-to-metres: far*near/(far-(far-near)*d).

execution.sense_shadow_from_render(shadow_boxel, target_pybullet_id, depth_image_m, seg_mask, view_matrix, projection_matrix, occluder_pybullet_ids=None, robot_id=None, support_body_ids=None) -> (outcome, blocked_fraction, detected_bodies, blocked_bbox, interceptor_counts).

execution.compute_shadow_blockers(camera_pos, registry, shadow_ids, object_ids, env) -> Dict[shadow_id, List[object_boxel_id]]; needs env.detect_objects, env._depth_buffer_to_meters, env._view_and_projection_matrices, env.objects.

execution.execute_pick(robot_id, env, obj_name, obj_pos, grasp, config, gui, obj_aabb=(min,max), _retry=False) -> (held_body_id|None, RobotConfig|None); execute_place(robot_id, env, obj_name, place_pos, grasp, config, held_body_id, gui, held_aabb) -> RobotConfig|None (raises EmptyHandError); execute_stack(robot_id, env, obj_name, on_obj_name, grasp, config, held_body_id, gui, held_aabb, support_aabb) -> RobotConfig|None.

execution.handle_sense_action(action_params=(obj, shadow_id), env, registry, belief, viz, target_name, robot_id, support_body_ids, shadows, occluders, shadow_occluder_map, blocked_counts, blocked_giveup_shadows, nontarget_rediscovery_counts, boxel_centers, boxel_to_pybullet, object_body_ids, body_id_to_name, show_free) -> ActionResult(continue_, reason).

execution.world_integrity_check(env, registry, belief, viz, shadows, occluders, shadow_occluder_map, boxel_centers, on_relations, held_name, label) -> (events, dets, render); register_new_detections(env, registry, belief, viz, detections, target_name, shadows, occluders, shadow_occluder_map, boxel_centers, boxel_to_pybullet, object_body_ids, render=None, skip_names) -> List[name]; refresh_object_aabbs(env, registry, viz, detections, render, check_lost, exclude_ids) -> lost ids.

PDDLStreamPlanner(registry, robot_id=plan_robot_id, shadow_occluder_map, physics_client=plan_client_id, object_body_ids (plan-side ids keyed by name AND boxel id), support_body_ids (plan-side plane+table), camera_pos, tray_name); BoxelStreams reads the robot base pose from the plan client at construction for the reach gate.

robot_utils constants: ARM_JOINT_INDICES [0..6], FINGER_JOINTS [9,10], END_EFFECTOR_LINK 11, _PANDA_IGNORED_SELF_PAIRS {(-1,0),(0,1),...,(10,11)}, _PANDA_GRIPPER_LINKS {6,7,8,9,10,11}, JOINT_LIMITS_LOW/HIGH, REST_POSES [0,-0.785,0,-2.356,0,1.571,0.785], JOINT_VELOCITY_LIMITS, SIM_TIMESTEP 1/240, MAX_INTERP_STEPS 1200, IK_ORN_TOL_DEG 10, FK gate 10 mm with 2 refinement rounds; open target 0.04 (160 steps, 200 N), close force 60 N, close_gripper_until_contact(step 0.0005, max_steps 240, squeeze 0.003), move_robot_smooth(steps=60 default, 30 per waypoint in the dispatcher, force 240, settle hold up to 120 steps at 2e-3 rad). Duplicated literals: boxel_env.py:735 (link 11), :810/:824 (links 9,10, friction 1.2, reset 0.04); world_eye.EE_LINK 11, FINGER_JOINTS (9,10); telemetry ee_link=11.

Camera (ours): eye [0.1,-0.8,0.7], target [0.1,0,0.5], up [0,0,1], 640x480, fov 60, near 0.01, far 5.0; view/proj via p.computeViewMatrix / computeProjectionMatrixFOV; TINY renderer for detection, OpenGL only for GUI panes. Camera (theirs): hand-mounted link camera_frame, 640x480, fx=fy=525 (vertical fov about 49 deg), OpenGL renderer, moved by look actions.

Table/workspace (ours): top z 0.325, logical ranges x(-0.4,0.6) y(-0.5,0.5) for shadows, _SAFE x(-0.1,0.70) y(-0.40,0.40) for free space and on_surface, robot base at (-0.4,0,0). Table/workspace (theirs): top z 0.0, table 1.53x1.22 at x=0.1 (shortened 0.75x1.22 at x=0.475), objects x in [0.3,0.7] y in [-0.4,0.4], robot at origin, visibility grid x from 0.37 to table_upper-0.05, z top+0.02 to top+0.1, voxel 15 mm (GRID_RESOLUTION 0.02 in panda_env_utils.py:79 is a different constant).

Reach (ours, measured for base at z 0.05): REACH_LIMIT_M 0.80, REACH_SPHERE_CENTER_Z_WORLD 0.066, REACH_SPHERE_R_M 0.815; spawn-time _PANDA_REACH_RADIUS 0.65. For a base at z 0 the sphere centre must be re-expressed as base_z + 0.016 or re-measured with tools/_probe_reach_envelope.py in their world.

Grasp/size priors: _GRASP_Z_OFFSETS [0.10, 0.06], GRASP_MAX_SPAN 0.076, GRASP_SQUARE_TOL 0.005, altitude gate half_height + 0.01, NOMINAL_HIDDEN_EXTENTS 0.04, NOMINAL_HIDDEN_EXTENTS_MIN 0.03, contact_z = max(top - 0.005, table_z + 0.035), pre-grasp aperture pinch_half + 0.008 capped at 0.04, width gate [0.005, pinch_half + 0.008], post-action lift 0.10.

ShadowCalculator(camera_position, table_surface_height, table_x_range, table_y_range).calculate_shadow_boxel(obj_boxel, obstacles, physics_client=None): mid-air rule (bottom > table + 0.01 casts nothing), horizontal-plane back corners, 5 m rays into the TRUE world on the default client, hits clamped to the table ranges, then two-slab carve and obstacle subtraction.

TAMPURA success criterion: holding the die AND at-home (go-home action); our harness scores holding by held id equality plus a pad-contact check and has no at-home clause; TAMPURA sweep fields per seed: success, wall_s, loop_s, solve_step, n_actions, rewards (sweep_2026-05-26.json, not read here).

TAMPURA scene files: tampura_environments/find_dice/problems/*.json with {'categories': [...], 'poses': [...]}; categories are 'dice' plus a_cups_ud..e_cups_ud; YCB meshes created with create_ycb(name, use_concave=True) via trimesh and createMultiBody; env.get_scene_data picks a file with random.choice, so seed-for-seed means seeding that choice exactly as their sweep driver did.
honesty_risks: ShadowCalculator raycasts the TRUE physics world (shadow_calculator.py:160) when casting a believed object's shadow; on their scene a ray could terminate on a body the robot has not observed and shrink or shape a fragment from privileged geometry. PAPER_AUDIT item (h) is still open; the bridge plan must either accept and disclose it, cast the rays in the belief-posed plan client (physics_client=env.plan_client_id, already a parameter), or replace the raycast with pure table-plane projection.

Containment under a cup is not a lateral shadow: the die's cell is the cup footprint, which the camera sees from outside only as the cup. Any 'look underneath' fix must be a model tweak (a belief region cast by hollow-class objects, cleared by relocation plus observation), never a rule like 'if cup then pick it', and never seeded from the die's true pose. The archived bridge's camera placement over the occluder centroid (perception_adapter.py:88-90) shows the right discipline: the fixed camera must be placed from the cups or the table, not from the die.

Static filtering by hardcoded names ('plane','table','robot') and the is_occluder / is_tray flags: a bridge that labels cups is_occluder=True and the die as target is fine only if the labels come from CLASS knowledge (the task says 'find the die', cups are the manipulable class); labelling must not depend on which cup actually covers the die.

ObjectInfo.size feeds auto_cell (test_full_pipeline.py:509-518). For YCB meshes the bridge must take sizes from a design-time class table or the perception estimate, not from p.getAABB of the live body (which would leak the instance's true pose-dependent AABB and the die's size while it is hidden).

NOMINAL_HIDDEN_EXTENTS 0.04 / 0.03 encode '3-4 cm cubes'. Re-parameterising them for the die class is honest only as a declared class prior (the die's nominal size from the task spec), not measured from the hidden instance; GRASP_MAX_SPAN 0.076 vs cup diameters may make some cups ungraspable top-down, which must then end as an honest failure or a disclosed sampler change (H3), not a weld or a scripted side grasp.

Sense grid geometry (dense slice at base + 0.02 m) assumes targets >= 3 cm tall; a die under 2 cm cannot be hit by the grid even when the fragment is clear. Discovery then relies on register_new_detections after the cup moves (the F20 path), which is legitimate; the plan must state this and must not add a grid tweak tuned to the die's true position.

Default-client coupling: execution.py and robot_utils motion/gripper functions address pybullet's default client. TAMPURA opens two BulletClients (world and sim_world). If our physics calls land on their belief world by accident the robot would act on and read a world that is not the executing one. Threading physicsClientId through is mechanical but must be done or the first-connection order must be guaranteed and asserted.

The plan client mirror: a bridge needs a DIRECT twin with the same URDF and YCB meshes so plan_body_id works; the twin must be posed from the belief (sync_to_plan_client with registry), never from their world's true poses, or the planner plans against ground truth (PAPER_AUDIT item (j)).

Phase 4 oracle hidden split and target choice (test_full_pipeline.py:692-744) are harness-only but run inside main(); for find_dice the target is fixed by class, so the bridge must set target_name = the die symbol without reading its visibility, and visible_target_locations must come from the registry only (as :750-753 already does).

Loop termination compares held_body_id with env.objects[target].object_id (identity via the accepted seg-id recognition map). This equals TAMPURA's own seg-id-to-symbol identity (env.py:64-75), so parity holds, but the plan should state the shared assumption explicitly and must not extend it to poses (ours estimate from depth; theirs return true poses of visible bodies).

Dispatcher retry policies (one-shot grasp retry, 3-strike giveups and paroles, disposal plan, runtime plan_motion re-solve) are loop-level decision logic that already exists in the thesis pipeline; carrying them over is consistent, but adding any new retry or fallback tuned on their seeds would be scripted decision logic (H2) and must be flagged.

The hardcoded post-action lift is 0.10 m in code (execution.py:869, :1246) while the audit exemption text says ~5 cm after pick; the plan must disclose the actual value and must not grow it into an approach or transport motion.

Pre-flight comment 'seed lists must be pre-vetted' (test_full_pipeline.py:2468) and our scene generators' hidden-placement guarantees are OUR scene-side devices; with their 20 scene files none of it may be applied (no seed filtering, no re-roll, no winnability gate), per H4.

Scoring parity: TAMPURA's reward needs at-home after holding; our holding goal stops at the grasp. Either the bridge goal adds the home condition as a planned action or the comparison states the criterion difference; silently scoring 'holding' as their 'success' would overstate ours.

Timeouts: our runner marks a killed cell 'timeout' (run_logger.py:285-289) and the planner gets max_time 1800 s by default; TAMPURA's per-seed wall_s budgets differ. The plan must fix a common wall-clock budget before any number is quoted.

Their look-conf sampler reads the true pose of the object it looks behind (env.py:617) and their observation returns true poses of visible bodies (env.py:71-73); this is their system's own choice and must be recorded as a parity note, not imitated by ours.

Camera renderer parity: ours uses ER_TINY_RENDERER for detection; theirs uses OpenGL. Depth values differ slightly; the fixed external camera for our system inside their world must use our renderer path (identical headless and GUI pixels) and its pose must be recorded in the audit as a model parameter.
